finding: IMAGE_THEFT_OR_SCAM is unreachable on the production path
verified_by: src/searcher/ranking/vetoes.py:110 fires the veto only when stolen_photo is true
src/searcher/ranking/pipeline.py:100 sets stolen_ids = stolen or set()
the only caller that supplies `stolen` is searcher/workers/vision/worker.py
grep of src and tests shows run_vision_worker is referenced only from tests/integration
consequence: In production stolen_ids is always empty, so IMAGE_THEFT_OR_SCAM can never fire. A listing that reuses the brand's official photographs on a day-old account demanding off-platform payment scores item 0.91, authenticity 0.80, no veto, and publishes as Real.
other_false_reals_found: counterfeit using official stock photography -> Real (item 0.901125, auth 0.80)
counterfeit using a lookbook screenshot -> Real, and the screenshot RAISES authenticity to 0.88
stock_mixed=True still Real, because inserted-stock-photograph is not a hard contradiction
duplicate listing published twice as Real; DUPLICATE_NO_UTILITY is unused
why_the_benchmark_missed_it: The public benchmark prints false Real: 0, but that run supplies the oracle stolen flag and labels stock_mixed as truth real. It does not measure these shapes. The headline safety number is measuring around the failure it exists to catch.
user_harm: A buyer searching for a designer item can be routed to a scam listing marked Real - the strongest claim the product makes - on the strength of the brand's own photographs.
blocks: PUBLIC_ALPHA_READY and PRIVATE_ALPHA_READY. Not a scope limitation; a safety defect.
